# A product joins an installation, and the thing it generates is an application

**ID**: `cpt-gearbox-adr-installation-and-application`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Context and Problem Statement

A live pass over the Studio produced seven complaints. Six were defects and are
fixed. Three of them turned out to rest on the same thing, and it is not a
defect but a model: **the product is a closed world.**

A description names gears, the resolver takes the co-location closure, and the
generator emits a crate and a process for everything in it.
`crates/gearbox-engine/src/resolve/cuts.rs:87-95` states it without
apology — a provider outside the product "cannot satisfy anything, and treating
it as if it could would turn 'you did not select the provider' into a silently
working binding."

That is right for the first deployment and wrong for every one after it. A site
that already runs `types-registry`, an event broker and a directory does not
want them regenerated because somebody added one business gear. And several such
gears will share that site: many compositions, one `types-registry`, one broker.

### What the model has, and what it does not

`ProductIntent` has nine fields and none of them says "already running".
`SourceDecl` has exactly three variants — `path`, `git`, `registry` — and all
three answer *where the source is*, never *where it runs*.

Someone reached for the gap and the hand did not close. `bind(endpoint = ...)`
is in the language, is carried into the IR under a doc comment promising "a
pinned address, overriding whatever discovery would produce", and was **dropped
by the resolver**, which read only `mode` and `transport`. It refuses now
(GBX0411) rather than lying, which is a holding position this ADR is here to
replace.

The cluster scopes look like a precedent and are not. A backend named
`provider("postgres", connection_string = ...)` is plainly outside the product,
but it works precisely because **a cluster backend is not a gear**: no crate, no
process, no contract, no closure membership, so nobody ever had to decide
whether to generate it. The product still builds the `cluster` gear itself.

### The shared cluster is already broken, measurably

Not a naming complaint. `generate/helm.rs:653-659` deliberately does *not*
prefix Service names with the Helm release, because the lock dials neighbours at
`http://{subchart}.{namespace}.svc.cluster.local` and a prefix "would point
every consumer at a DNS name that answers nothing." So two products in one
namespace, each generating its own `types-registry`, emit two Services of the
same name. The closed world reaches the cluster.

### And the vocabulary is one level off

`ResolvedProcess` carries `replicas: u32`. A process does not have replicas — a
Deployment has pods, each running one process. The model has been calling the
*unit of deployment* a process, which is the same conflation as two of the
defects this pass found: a sentence attached to a node that made a claim about
an edge, and a reason for a gear that pointed at a profile.

Meanwhile there is no word at all for the level above: the running whole at one
site, into which several products are deployed.

## Decision Outcome

Four decisions, and they are one decision asked four times: what is a fact about
a gear, about a product, about an installation, and about the tree we emit.

### 1. A product may reference an installation, and greenfield stays the default

"Already deployed" is expressed as **a reference to another product's lock**.
The lock is the right artefact because it exists, is canonical, is ordered and
hashed, and records exactly what was resolved: which gears, which contracts,
which endpoints. Nothing new has to be *described*; only pointed at.

**Both modes are first-class and the greenfield one is the default.** Standing
up a whole ecosystem from nothing — several gears, everything generated — is not
a legacy path. It is how a first installation comes to exist, and it is what the
demo corpus and all 162 conformance claims do. The reference is therefore
**optional**: a product declaring none resolves, generates and behaves exactly
as it does today. That is the safety argument and also the regression test.

The two modes compose rather than compete: the first product builds the
installation, later ones join it. Note this dissolves the Service-name collision
above without inventing a naming scheme — a referenced gear generates no
Deployment and no Service, so nothing is left to collide.

#### How the reference is spelled, and why not by hash

**By path plus `profile_kind`, and not pinned by `lock_hash`.**

The profile *id* is the wrong key and the codebase already says so: it is the
only header field the lock differ throws away — `profile: _` at
`crates/gearbox-lock/src/diff.rs:326-350` — and ADR-0014 records the reason,
that the kind "is already treated as the meaningful identity". A profile id is a
free-form label unique only within one product, so A's `local` and B's `local`
are unrelated strings.

`lock_hash` is the wrong pin for a different reason: it is a blake3 over the
whole canonical body including `gearbox_version`
(`crates/gearbox-lock/src/canonical.rs:74-84`), so it moves on a toolchain bump
when nothing semantic changed. A pin that breaks on every upgrade is a pin
nobody keeps.

So the reference is to a *dependency*, not to a snapshot: the lock is re-read at
each resolution, and drift is simply the new answer. If a stronger guarantee is
wanted later, it needs a semantic hash that excludes `gearbox_version` — which
does not exist and should not be invented speculatively.

**Amended 2026-09-12, before any of this was built: that question is now
answered, and the answer demotes `profile_kind` from a key to a check.**
ADR-0014 has chosen the shape in which two profiles may select one target, so a
kind identifies a *family* and never a resolution. The reference is therefore
keyed by **path** -- `.gearbox/<product>/<profile>/product.lock` already names
one resolution exactly, because the profile is the directory -- and
`profile_kind` is compared as a guard: a product resolving for Kubernetes and
pointing at an installation resolved as `embedded` is refused, while matching
kinds prove nothing beyond not being obviously wrong.

That is a weaker claim than the original paragraph made and the right one. It
also costs nothing today: profile work is deferred and new design assumes one
profile per product, so the ambiguity this guards against cannot yet arise. The
guard is here so that it is not forgotten when it can.

#### What a referenced gear contributes, and what it does not

It satisfies contracts and occupies the catalogue. It produces **no crate, no
application, no chart**. `InclusionReason` gains a variant for it, and
`generate/mod.rs`, which iterates every application with no filter, gains the
`skipped` list its own header says should return "the moment something can
genuinely be skipped, with a producer". This is that producer.

`GBX0301` must be relaxed from "the orchestrator is in this product" to "the
orchestrator is in the installation". One site is one installation is one
directory, and a flat directory namespace is correct there — the tenancy worry
that first looked like a blocker was a worry about sharing one directory between
*isolated* ecosystems, which is not this.

#### Version skew across the boundary gets its own refusal

The installation provides `SomeContract@v1` and a new gear consumes `@v2`.
Inside a closure that is GBX0405, whose remedy is "select the provider" — and
that remedy is useless here, because the provider is deployed and not the
integrator's to select.

**A new diagnostic refuses it**, naming both versions and the two things that
can actually be done: upgrade the installation, or take a gear built against the
version it offers. Not a warning: the runtime will not bind these, so a product
that resolved clean would fail at deploy — and a diagnostic that lets a person
find that out from Kubernetes is worse than one that stops them. This is the one
place where ADR-0013's "errors warn, they do not block" does not reach, because
there the warning describes something that *might* work.

### 2. `process` becomes `application`; `installation` is added; `product` waits

Four levels, and today's vocabulary names two:

| Level | Today | Decided |
|---|---|---|
| one unit of code | gear | gear |
| one binary, one Deployment, N replicas | **process** | **application** |
| a composition one team owns and ships | **product** | product, for now |
| the running whole at one site | *(no word)* | **installation** |

**`application` agrees with the platform rather than colliding with it.** The
public glossary (`docs/web-docs/introduction/glossary.md`) defines it as "what
assembles multiple gears into one runnable system", which is exactly this level;
that it has so far coincided with a whole product over there is a consequence of
the platform having one binary, not a difference in the definition. It also
agrees with `AppConfig`, which is already the configuration of one process, and
with `apps/`, which is already where a composed binary lives.

The near-miss considered and accepted: **"Application Gear"** is a
glossary-defined term for a business gear, contrasted with "System Gear" by who
wrote it rather than by containment. So "this application's application gears
and system gears" is awkward and true, and the platform's own `apps/` member
already has both.

**`installation` is free.** It is the one candidate with no existing owner: six
incidental prose uses and no definition, no type, no glossary entry. `estate`
and `deployment` are formal entities in `infrastructure-resource-manager` and
mean the *customer's* cloud resources; `environment` is the word ADR-0014
warns against, since profile ids "read as an environment axis. They are not."

**`product` is not renamed now, and not because it is safe.** `service`, the
obvious candidate, turns out to be taken *at the wrong level*: the platform's
own documents say "each service is an out-of-process gear plus the system gears
it depends on", which is nearer this model's application than its product. And
decision 1 changes what this level *is* — today a description generates the
whole closure, afterwards it generates its own part and references the rest — so
the concept is moving and naming it before it settles is the wrong order.
`product.gdl` and `product.lock` are on-disk names in every description,
document and test, which makes this a migration with a compatibility story
rather than a rename.

### 3. The output layout is configurable, default `apps/`

The precedent is close and already accepted: `product(templates = ...)` lets a
description override the generator's Jinja templates, so "the product may
reconfigure what the generator emits" is settled. The layout setting sits beside
it, at product level rather than profile level — a directory name is a fact
about the tree, and the tree is per product, while `target_dir`,
`cargo_profile`, `namespace` and `image_registry` are per profile because each
names something the profile decides.

Default `apps/`, overridable to `processes/` so an existing checkout can keep
its shape.

Two hazards, both recorded because neither is obvious. **The keying has to move
together**: renaming the directory alone would leave `apps/api-gateway/` holding
package `gbx-gateway` beside `config/gateway.yaml` — three spellings of one
thing, which is worse than what exists. And `generate/apply.rs` has **no prune
step**, so a layout change leaves the old tree next to the new one, and a stale
`processes/<p>/Cargo.toml` inside the generated workspace is exactly what
`generate/workspace.rs:51-58` exists to prevent.

### 4. In-process-only is derived; features are curated then scoped

**Derived, not declared, and no change to `#[toolkit::gear]`.** `grpc-hub`
cannot run alone: its registration API is `Box<dyn Fn(&mut RoutesBuilder)>`
handed through an `Arc` in one address space
(`libs/toolkit/src/contracts.rs:189`), so there is no wire form and a hub in its
own process is a running, empty server whose former co-tenants fail at startup.
`api-gateway` is the same shape for REST.

The IR cannot say this today: it has `colocated_deps` (a relation between two
gears) and `RuntimeCap::is_process_singleton()` (at most one per process) and
nothing between. But the two singleton caps are **exactly** `RestHost | GrpcHub`
(`crates/gearbox-ir/src/catalogue.rs:88-90`), which are exactly the two
in-process registration hosts — so the property follows from facts already
projected, and ADR-0002's rule that overlapping facts are projected rather than
restated stays intact.

The test that would overturn this is recorded so the question is not reopened by
taste: extend the macro when the corpus produces a case that is **not**
derivable from caps. It has not. Plugins are covered by GBX0514, and
`types-registry` is ubiquitous by frequency rather than by constraint.

> **Amendment 2026-09-15: the condition above has been met, and the macro is
> extended.** A gear that may exist only once in an installation --
> `service-discovery`, whose directory is one process's in-memory map -- is not
> derivable from capabilities. The set is closed at seven, each backed by a
> trait the gear macro asserts, so an eighth would need a trait invented for it;
> and the property is about the installation rather than the process, which is a
> different quantifier from `is_process_singleton`. So
> `#[toolkit::gear(one_per_installation = true)]` is added and projected, exactly
> as this decision said should happen in this case. See ADR
> `cpt-gearbox-adr-one-per-installation`, which also records why the intuitive
> form of the constraint -- "linked into at most one application" -- is the wrong
> question.

**Features are two problems and the order matters.** They were being discarded
entirely — `GearSelection.features` was read by nothing — which is fixed, and
had to be first, because scoping a value that is thrown away would be scoping
nothing.

*Which features to offer* is the `exposes_features` counterpart to `exposes`,
declared in `gear.gdl` per ADR-0002; `CrateManifest`'s own doc already names the
gap, that the projection is "every name, uncurated" and curation "is a
declaration … and there is no such declaration yet". Today the wizard offers
`integration` (wants a Docker daemon), `test-support`, `fips` and the literal
string `default`. **This is a cross-repo commitment**: all fourteen `gear.gdl`
files live in `gears-rust`, on its `feature/gearbox` branch, and while there is
precedent — `exposes` is already ours — it has to be agreed rather than assumed.

> **Decision 1's mechanism is superseded by ADR-0018.** "Already deployed" is
> declared with `installation(...)` rather than read out of another product's
> lock: `platform-host` — the installation that matters most — is deployed by the
> platform's own chart and has no Gearbox lock to point at. The reasoning below
> was sound; the ground moved. ADR-0018 also states the rule this ADR is missing,
> that only a gear reached across a *contract* edge can be referenced at all,
> because `deps` are link-time.

> **Both halves landed, and the second did not need the language change.**
> `gear(cargo_features = [...])` carries the curation *and* the scope:
> `feature("k8s-auth", kinds = ["kubernetes"])`. The cross-repo agreement was
> taken — seven `gear.gdl` files on `feature/gearbox` declare one, and the other
> seven declare no Cargo features to curate.
>
> The scoping avoided `use_gear(profiles = ...)` by turning the question around.
> A product scoping its own choice by profile would be the language change
> feared below; a **gear** declaring which deployment kinds its own feature
> belongs to is a fact about the gear, and the resolution only reports the
> contradiction (`GBX0316`). ADR-0014's "never a selection" rule is amended
> there rather than here, and only in that direction.
>
> What it does *not* do is let one product enable a feature for `prod` and not
> for `dev`: `use_gear` still takes no `profiles`, so a feature is selected for
> every profile, and a product declaring an embedded profile simply cannot ask
> for `k8s-auth` at all. That is why `validate` checks every declared profile
> and not just the one being resolved.

*Scoping a choice to a profile* is a language change: `use_gear` takes no
`profiles`, and only `plugin`, `bind`, `cluster_profile` and `application` are
scopable. ADR-0014 closes the shortcut in advance — `kind()` "feeds the lock
header, CLI text and Studio labels — and never a selection" — so scoping stays
an enumeration of ids, with the same weakness the reference matching inherits.

## Consequences

* A second product in the corpus becomes necessary, not optional: "joining"
  cannot be observed with one. It is part of the work.
* The greenfield path must stay byte-identical, which is a stronger constraint
  than "still passes" and is what the existing suite is for.
* Two locks may disagree about a contract and the tool now says so. That is new
  surface for an operator to meet, and the wording of one diagnostic is what
  stands between "helpful" and "blocked for reasons I cannot act on".
* `application` is one word away from "application gear" in every sentence. The
  documents will need care that the code does not.
* Renaming `process` touches 180 occurrences, four generated TypeScript types,
  the GDL `process(...)` constructor, and `[[process]]` in the lock. Existing
  locks are regenerable, so the format change is a cost rather than a migration
  — but `lock_hash` stability has been protected deliberately here before, and
  this breaks every existing hash at once.
* `product` keeps a name that is one level too high for a shared cluster, and
  knowingly, until decision 1 settles what it denotes.

## Confirmation

* The greenfield claim is the existing suite, unchanged: 162 claims, and a
  product declaring no reference must generate what it generates today.
* The joining claim needs the second product: referenced gears produce no crate,
  no application and no Service, and a consumer still resolves.
* The version-skew refusal is checked on a fixture, since the corpus has one
  product and no version disagreement to find.
* In-process-only is confirmed by a test that isolating `grpc-hub` into a worker
  is refused, and by its `prevents` reference to `RegistryError::GrpcRequiresHub`
  resolving under `GEARBOX_CORPUS_REQUIRED=1` — the mechanism ADR-0015
  introduced, applied to its own case.
* The layout change is confirmed by generating both ways and diffing the trees,
  and by the absence of a stale `processes/` beside a new `apps/`.

## Traceability

* Refines `cpt-gearbox-fr-explain` and `cpt-gearbox-nfr-explainability`
  indirectly: a referenced gear's inclusion reason is a new answer to "why is
  this here".
* **Will relax** the rule GBX0301 enforces (`resolve/structural.rs:212-228`).
* **Will retire** the holding position GBX0411 took (`resolve/bindings.rs`),
  which refuses a declared endpoint until this decision exists.

> **Both are future tense, and were written in the past tense by mistake.**
> Neither has happened: GBX0411 is still an error and its help text still tells
> an operator "Pointing at a provider outside the product is not expressible
> yet", and GBX0301 still says a gear is "not in the catalogue". An ADR that
> claims a change it has not made is worse than one that claims nothing, because
> the next reader stops checking.
>
> **Decisions 2, 3 and 4 have landed** — `application`, the configurable `apps/`
> layout with GBX0706 for the tree it leaves behind, and `cargo_features` with
> GBX0213 and GBX0316. **Decision 1 — `installation` — has not been started.**
> Nothing in `crates/` mentions it, `product(...)` takes no reference to another
> lock, `InclusionReason` still has its three original variants, the version-skew
> diagnostic does not exist, and the corpus still holds one product where this
> decision's Consequences call a second one "necessary, not optional". Until that
> work happens, this ADR stays `proposed`.
* Extends ADR-0002: a referenced lock is a locator, and what is read out of it
  is projected rather than restated.
* Was blocked by ADR-0014's open question about two profiles of one kind in
  exactly one place, the reference matching rule; that question is answered in
  ADR-0014's 2026-09-12 amendment and the rule is corrected above.
* Respects ADR-0010: `gears-rust` is read, never written, except for the
  `exposes_features` field which is called out above as a cross-repo agreement.
* Answers the scenario that `docs/PRD.md` §4.2 and
  `docs/vision.md` §111 leave in neither scope nor non-goals,
  and realises for gears what the vision's §54 already asks for infrastructure:
  "integrate into an existing cluster rather than always deploying bundled
  dependencies".
